transcript: Yesterday, I saw a new play by Preston Max Allen called Caroline, and it was a heavy one. We first see a young mother at a diner with her trans, fourth grade daughter in the aftermath of a really harmful situation. We learn about the mother's troubling past, her past with her own mother, and how it all complicates how she's supposed to handle this undeniably destabilizing and precarious situation. I don't want to reveal too much because I think it's best to just experience how it unfolds, but I would definitely recommend this one. It was very captivating and I was invested in the story and the characters, but I actually wasn't viscerally reactive throughout, despite it depicting objectively devastating circumstances. Maybe it was the aesthetic of the production, which was efficiently designed but felt a little cold and detached to me. Nonetheless, the performances and the character relationships felt really authentic, and the themes of motherhood, trust, and protection were sharply rendered. I was left thinking about the fragility of life and safety and theoretically unbreakable bonds. Like a lot of good theater, Caroline is complex and deeply human. With that, another program for my collection.
